instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: The root is closed to unlisted properties and requires schema_id, project, generatedAt, coverageLevel, and items.
atoms.title: Closed root with mandatory strategy fields

atoms.statement: The items array must be nonempty, each item rejects unlisted fields, and seven core test-definition fields are mandatory.
atoms.title: Nonempty closed test-item records

atoms.statement: coverageLevel accepts exactly Basic, Standard, or Comprehensive.
atoms.title: Three-level coverage vocabulary

atoms.statement: The schema centralizes reference values in $defs.ref as strings with minimum length one and closes the root document after that definition.
atoms.title: Shared nonempty reference primitive

atoms.statement: testFile, testName, and verificationCommand are constrained only as nonempty strings; the schema defines no command grammar, allowlist, execution authority, working directory, timeout, exit-code oracle, or path boundary.
atoms.title: Executable command and file locator lack safety contract

atoms.statement: The three coverage labels are not coupled to conditional item counts, test categories, capability coverage, provenance, evidence, or other measurable completeness criteria.
atoms.title: Comprehensive coverage is not structurally falsifiable

atoms.statement: id and sourcePhaseId are only nonempty strings; the items array has no uniqueItems constraint and the schema provides no identifier pattern or cross-artifact referential-integrity rule.
atoms.title: Item and phase identities are not integrity-checked

atoms.statement: All three reference families and evidencePath are optional, reference arrays have no minimum size or uniqueness requirement, and $defs.ref guarantees only a nonempty string rather than an existing authorized target.
atoms.title: Evidence and provenance closure are optional and unresolved

atoms.statement: exampleOnly is optional and has no declared default or behavioral relationship to coverage, verification, or evidence, creating three representable states with only two named meanings.
atoms.title: Optional exampleOnly flag has undefined absent state

atoms.statement: generatedAt relies on the date-time format keyword, but the schema does not declare or otherwise enforce a consumer-wide format-assertion policy.
atoms.title: Timestamp rejection semantics depend on validator configuration

atoms.statement: The schema sets minimum sizes but no maxItems, maxLength, or aggregate payload limit for test items, references, or free-text fields.
atoms.title: Strategy payload has no scale bounds

cross_document_questions: Which canonical consumer executes verificationCommand, and what allowlist, sandbox, working-directory, timeout, and exit-code contract constrains it?
Which canonical owner defines uniqueness and referential integrity for item id, sourcePhaseId, methodResearchRefs, installationReceiptRefs, and requiredCapabilityRefs?
Where are Basic, Standard, and Comprehensive translated into measurable coverage obligations that make the declared level falsifiable?
Is test_strategy.schema.json intentionally only a planning artifact, or must another canonical receipt prove execution outcome and bind evidencePath to immutable evidence?
research_seed_queries: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 format annotation versus assertion portability for date-time
secure representation and sandboxed execution of machine-readable test verification commands
schema patterns for referential integrity and evidence provenance in test strategy artifacts

atoms.statement: The prologue establishes immutable canonical UsageRecord aggregation, shared runtime attribution, provider-specific evidence classes, source-qualified GUI labels, canonical placement, durable pressure/switch history, and rollup-backed retention behavior while keeping provider/runtime facts outside Usage ownership.
atoms.title: Canonical usage truth, ownership, and provider evidence are explicitly separated

atoms.statement: UF-002 through UF-004 make Usage a first-class implementation-agnostic GUI feature, bind its values to seglog-derived redb rollups rather than usage.jsonl, and require object-first project/run/package/lane and usage_event_ref routing instead of timestamp, tier, or thread shortcuts.
atoms.title: Usage envelope, rollup source, and routing identity are addressable

atoms.statement: UF-005 through UF-011 distinguish export classes, preserve projection-trust and blocked ownership, retain switch/pressure lineage, constrain widget consumers, expose source-qualified quota and ledger analytics, and route thread detail through an explicit context-circle interaction rather than a second Usage surface.
atoms.title: Export, trust, account, widget, quota, ledger, and chat contracts are preserved

atoms.statement: UF-012 through UF-018 define curated thread inspection and estimated-cost caveats, then preserve provider-specific Cursor, Codex, Copilot, and Claude account, billing, entitlement, and source-evidence boundaries instead of flattening them into a universal quota model.
atoms.title: Thread inspection and provider-specific usage evidence remain distinct

atoms.statement: UF-019 through UF-025 separate direct Gemini from retired Gemini CLI lineage, make direct setup API-key-specific, constrain active family pooling by effective capability, expose source confidence and reset truth, prevent status probes from becoming quota evidence, and keep cost_usage routing on the canonical usage schema.
atoms.title: Gemini retirement, active pooling, source confidence, probes, and artifact routing are separated

atoms.statement: UF-026 through UF-032 retain OpenCode only as a non-binding reference, establish canonical backend input precedence, prevent Usage-linked widgets from owning plan state, fix the canonical surfaces, require immutable attributed usage events, constrain Debug phase labels to analytics, and preserve a shared billing attribution family.
atoms.title: Normalization, consumer boundaries, placement, immutable events, and billing attribution are explicit

atoms.statement: UF-033 through UF-039 define object-first inspector routing, projection-health and quiet-window rules, canonical alias normalization, cost precision boundaries, blocked escalation observability, missing-secret fallback labels, and rate-limited refresh behavior.
atoms.title: Inspector, projection health, schema aliases, cost, blocking, fallback, and refresh are addressable

atoms.statement: The prologue explicitly requires pre-execution disclosure for non-reversible and non-undoable actions, records undo-window semantics, and preserves parent/child bulk results instead of flattening partial failures.
atoms.title: Cost-bearing destructive actions and bulk receipts have explicit reversibility disclosure

atoms.statement: UF-023 explicitly distinguishes authoritative native quota, authoritative session/tool stats, and inferred usage, and requires unknown reset/cooldown copy instead of fabricated countdowns.
atoms.title: Provider source confidence and unknown reset states cannot be fabricated

atoms.statement: The prologue defines rolling, fixed-reset, billing-cycle, session-only, and unknown window kinds plus scope and label fields, including a rule that unknown windows may be shown only with qualified evidence.
atoms.title: The generic usage-window state model is explicit

atoms.statement: The plan fixes v1 to current-project usage and acknowledges that any future all-project scope requires an explicit selector and a specified discovery topology; no all-project storage or permission contract exists in this assignment.
atoms.title: Cross-project aggregation remains intentionally unresolved

atoms.statement: The plan correctly says a generic 5h/7d column is misleading, yet UF-009 canonically requires always-visible 5h and 7d windows without conditioning them on provider availability or mapping them through window_kind/window_label. A builder can satisfy UF-009 literally and violate the generic usage-window contract.
atoms.title: Always-visible 5h/7d wording conflicts with provider-specific window semantics

atoms.statement: The enhancement permits a separate alerts file even though the canonical pipeline requires one UsageRecord write/read model and classifies usage.jsonl as a mirror. It does not say whether alert episodes are canonical events, projections, retention-coupled records, or compatibility-only data.
atoms.title: Optional alerts.jsonl would reintroduce a parallel usage-side state owner

atoms.statement: The plan names a 90-day raw-event policy, compaction, optional export-first behavior, and retention/privacy controls, but it does not define who can change retention, whether archive is encrypted, whether deletion reaches projections/blobs/exports, how legal or audit holds behave, or how interrupted compaction rolls back.
atoms.title: Retention and privacy controls lack deletion, archive, and recovery semantics

atoms.statement: The widget addendum allows every widget to be removed and only guarantees a nonempty first load. It does not preserve a required quota/status widget, define an empty-state recovery action, or reconcile removal with the success criterion that 5h/7d is always visible.
atoms.title: Users can remove every Usage widget despite an always-visible/default contract

atoms.statement: The only responsive rule bottoms out at two columns below 1200px. No phone-width one-column breakpoint, minimum card width, overflow behavior, touch reordering, or reduced-density fallback is defined.
atoms.title: Responsive layout has no one-column or narrow-touch contract

atoms.statement: The export taxonomy precisely separates record, bundle, and view exports and requires trust disclosure, but it never defines who may export raw records/blobs, which secrets or personal fields are redacted, how missing refs are represented, or whether large bundle creation is atomic/resumable.
atoms.title: Export classes omit authorization, redaction, completeness, and size-failure behavior

atoms.statement: The canonical interaction requires hover to reveal actions and reserves direct click for Compact Now, while direct click may not open detail. The plan does not define focus, keyboard, screen-reader, touch, long-press, or reduced-motion equivalents, so some users cannot reach More Details without violating the canonical click behavior.
atoms.title: Hover/click split has no keyboard, touch, or assistive-technology equivalent

atoms.statement: UF-011 requires explicit choice and visible failure/degraded feedback, but does not define the state while compaction is running, whether repeated clicks coalesce, how cancellation works, what partial compaction means, or when retry is safe.
atoms.title: Compact Now lacks in-flight, duplicate-dispatch, retry, and rollback semantics

atoms.statement: UF-009 exposes rate-limit-hit actions to switch platform or pause, but does not say who owns the mutation, whether the action is run-scoped or policy-scoped, how capability and account eligibility are revalidated, what confirmation is needed, or what wins if pressure recovers while the user acts.
atoms.title: Switch-platform and pause actions lack authority and race preconditions

atoms.statement: UF-012 exposes raw payload toggles and per-message drill-down but does not define secret/PII redaction, project trust requirements, role-based access, payload size truncation, safe rendering of untrusted strings, or audit logging for disclosure.
atoms.title: Raw payload inspection has no redaction, size, trust, or access boundary

atoms.statement: UF-021 forbids creating active Gemini CLI rows and pressure signals and calls the evidence retired, but does not say how already-persisted active rows, rollups, cached eligibility, saved pools, or deep links are migrated, tombstoned, or surfaced during upgrade.
atoms.title: Retired Gemini CLI rows have no migration or invalidation procedure

atoms.statement: UF-022 lists capability and recovery disclosures and requires effective capabilities to satisfy the request, but does not define capability evidence version/freshness, how stale capability changes invalidate a pending save, or whether policy and preferred-provider updates commit atomically.
atoms.title: Family-pooling capability posture lacks freshness and atomic-save semantics

atoms.statement: UF-030 requires immutable records and corrections through a new version, but does not define correction_of/supersedes linkage, winner selection, replay idempotency, duplicate emission handling, ordering across concurrent writers, or how rollups reverse the prior value.
atoms.title: Immutable correction records lack supersession and idempotency semantics

atoms.statement: UF-031 permits five phase labels but does not define who assigns them, whether an event may span phases, how retries or concurrent helpers inherit phase, or what value represents unclassified and future phases. Analytics from different emitters can therefore be incomparable.
atoms.title: Debug phase attribution has no classification oracle

atoms.statement: The plan names rate cards, surcharges, and pricing snapshot metadata, but does not decide whether historical cost is frozen at event time, recalculated after a price correction, or represented by a correction record; it also omits the rule for unavailable, overlapping, or non-USD price rows.
atoms.title: Pricing evidence lacks an event-time selection and repricing transition rule

atoms.statement: The prologue says usage_id resolves to usage_record_id or usage_event_ref according to the importing source, and UF-035 requires normalization before persistence and routing, but no source discriminator or rejection rule decides which target applies when both or neither are present.
atoms.title: usage_id normalization is source-dependent without a deterministic discriminator

atoms.statement: UF-036 defines decimal places at USD thresholds, but not rounding mode, negative credits/refunds, zero, very large values, integer overflow, non-USD minor units, decimal separators, currency placement, or accessible spoken labels.
atoms.title: Cost display precision omits rounding, sign, overflow, currency, and locale rules

atoms.statement: The prologue says blocked/recovery flows use ordered allowed_action_ids[] and only allowed_actions[] is legacy, but UF-037 labels allowed_action_ids[] itself as a stale-token disposition. These statements cannot both guide a builder or validator.
atoms.title: allowed_action_ids[] is simultaneously current and retired

atoms.statement: UF-038 tells the UI to mention ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN and provide fallback data, but does not define secure acquisition, storage source, scope, permission checks, redaction in raw payloads/logs/exports, rotation, revocation, or distinction between missing and invalid credentials.
atoms.title: Secret-dependent provider data has labels but no secure secret lifecycle

atoms.statement: UF-039 requires reasonable cached intervals and explicit Refresh, but does not define one in-flight request per provider/account, rate-limit backoff and jitter, cancellation, offline versus missing-secret versus provider-error states, cache partitioning, response ordering, or whether an older response may overwrite a newer run-derived update.
atoms.title: Refresh lacks coalescing, backoff, offline, cache-scope, and stale-response rules

atoms.statement: UF-033 correctly forbids eager dereference, but does not define the UI and audit result when a ref is deleted, corrupt, too large, unauthorized, from an untrusted provider, or changes between row render and click.
atoms.title: On-demand inspector dereference has no unavailable, unauthorized, or hostile-blob behavior

atoms.statement: UF-034 lists current, refreshing, stale, degraded, and unavailable and requires record-backed fallback, but does not define entry/exit conditions, freshness thresholds, concurrent refresh precedence, whether stale can still authorize sensitive actions, or which evidence proves recovery.
atoms.title: Projection-health labels lack transition and recovery oracles
